things.note: A row of small circles labelled FE; no iron object or surface, only the chemical symbol in circles. Earlier a box with the word IRON.
A box with the word WATER; later a plain dark ellipse stands in for the drop, with no water look (no shine, no transparency).
Three pairs of dark dots above the drop; known only by convention, the narration and a heading says oxygen. Earlier a box with the word OXYGEN.
A flat dark brown ellipse sitting on the FE row, unlike a drop.
Small orange dots drifting from the atoms.
The FE circles look identical before and after giving up electrons; nothing is drawn as an ion or marked charged.
Grey-brown blobs gather along the lower edge of the drop; not recognisable as rust and not coloured orange-red.
Only a headline of words; the picture does not change in a way that shows pores or water passing.

changes.note: Orange dots peel off the atoms and move away.
The FE circles do not change at all.
Electron dots drift up through the drop toward the pairs of dots above, though the transfer is hard to follow and the dots fade out.

changes.change: Ions join with oxygen and water
changes.note: Grey blobs appear and slide in along the drop's lower edge, but nothing visibly joins together.
The grey blobs accumulate in a row along the lower edge of the drop; the change is a colour/blob build-up, not recognisable as rust.
Only text; the picture shows no flakes or pores.

changes.change: Water gets through the rust to more iron
changes.note: Only text and a few tiny orange dots at the bottom; no visible water passing through.
The picture holds almost still from 20 to 28 s, so it does not show ongoing rusting.
